name: Gävle
title: Gävle Container Feeder Gauging | Ship Thickness Measurement
description: Ship thickness measurement in Gävle for container feeders, forest product carriers and tankers: hatch covers, ballast tanks, ice belt and scrubber piping.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement for Feeders, Tankers and Forest Product Ships in Gävle
intro: Gävle is the largest container port on Sweden's east coast and a long-established outlet for timber, pulp, paper and other cargo from central Sweden. Feeder container ships run regular loops to the North Sea hubs, forest product carriers load at Granudden, and tankers bring fuels and chemicals to the energy port, all on the Bothnian Sea, where winter ice is part of the calendar. Atlantis sends its technicians from India for each assignment, timing their arrival to the ship's confirmed berth window.

highlights.h: Feeder loops with fixed berth windows
highlights.p: Container feeders linking Gävle with North Sea hubs call on regular schedules. Hatch covers, coamings, scrubber lines and a few ballast tanks can be gauged inside one berth window, and a larger scope can be spread over successive calls on the same loop.

Ships loading sawn timber, pulp and paper at the Granudden terminal take heavy unit loads on their tank tops and side structure. Hold and tank-top readings during loading show the wear before it turns into steel renewal at the next docking.

highlights.h: Bothnian Sea ice and the ice belt
highlights.p: In cold winters Gävle Bay can ice over, and ships then sail under traffic restrictions with icebreaker assistance. Spring gauging of the ice belt, bow and forefoot captures abrasion and indent damage while the crew still remember where the ship took the ice.

port.h: Gävle's container, forest and energy terminals
p: Gävle lies at the southern end of the Gulf of Bothnia, on a wide bay of the Bothnian Sea where the Gävle River reaches the coast. The port's terminals stand close to the city, around the river mouth and along the bay, and ships reach them along a dredged and piloted fairway across open water. That position puts Gävle within easy reach of the rail and road network serving central Sweden, which is why so much cargo from the interior is shipped here rather than further south. As elsewhere in the Baltic there is no meaningful tide, and the water level at the quay varies with weather and season rather than by the hour, which keeps access arrangements steady through a call.

Three groups of terminal define the traffic. The container terminal, run by Yilport Gävle and expanded in recent years, handles feeder services to the large North Sea hubs and is the busiest box terminal on this coast. Granudden handles forest products and other bulk and breakbulk cargo, loading sawn timber, pulp and paper onto ships for European markets. The energy port receives tankers carrying oil products, chemicals and other liquid cargo for the region. Around these, general cargo ships and small bulk carriers call for industrial cargo, and many of the ships on these routes carry ice class because Gävle stays open through the winter. The feeder services in particular tie Gävle into the global container network, so the ships calling here change as lines rotate tonnage between trades.

Each group gives a different gauging window. Feeders keep to schedules and stay only as long as cargo work takes, so their scopes are short and repeatable, ideally split across several calls. Forest product ships stay for a loading that can take a day or more, enough to work through holds and prepare some ballast tanks. Tankers at the energy port work under terminal safety rules and offer access to ballast tanks, voids and deck structure. Ice decides the season: in a cold winter the bay freezes and arrivals depend on icebreaker capacity, so owners tend to plan larger scopes for the open-water months and use winter calls for work inside the hull. Ships idle in the port between employment are the exception, giving time for complete surveys in any season.

facilities.h: Gauging at Gävle's container terminal, Granudden and the energy port
p: All gauging in Gävle is done afloat, because there is no drydock here for seagoing ships. At the container terminal, the team works around crane operations: hatch covers and coamings are gauged when the covers are on the quay or between moves, scrubber wash-water and overboard lines are measured with the system stopped, and selected ballast tanks are entered if the crew can prepare them during the call. At Granudden, holds are gauged as they come free in the loading plan, and tank tops and side frames are recorded before cargo covers them.

The energy port has its own safety rules, and any work on a tanker there is agreed with the terminal and governed by the ship's permit-to-work system, usually limited to ballast tanks, voids and deck structure outside hazardous zones. Ships waiting in the bay for a berth can be boarded by launch for short deck scopes in good weather, arranged by the agent. Full renewal survey programmes are completed at the docking yard the owner selects, and readings taken in Gävle travel with the ship as the steel estimate and the starting point for the surveyor's close-up plan.
list: Yilport Gävle container terminal — hatch covers, coamings, scrubber piping and selected ballast tanks on feeders within the berth window.
Granudden — hold, tank-top and side-frame gauging on forest product carriers while timber, pulp or paper is loaded.
Energy port — ballast tank, void and deck readings on tankers during discharge, within terminal approval.
General cargo quays — hold and ballast tank measurements on short-sea ships serving local industry.
Anchorage in Gävle Bay — short deck and air-pipe scopes by launch on ships waiting for a berth, weather permitting.

context.h: Winter navigation and inspection rules at Gävle
p: Port state control in Gävle is carried out under the Paris MoU by the Swedish Transport Agency. Winter brings a separate set of rules: when ice forms in the Bothnian Sea, the Swedish Maritime Administration announces traffic restrictions for ports such as Gävle, setting a minimum Finnish-Swedish ice class and a minimum size for ships that will receive icebreaker assistance. A feeder or tanker that wants to keep its Gävle calls through a hard winter needs the right ice class on its certificate and a hull that still meets the strengthening the class was built to, which is why ice-belt condition matters commercially as well as for safety.

Container lines running feeders to Gävle are under pressure to cut emissions on short-sea legs, with the EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime now applying on voyages within Europe, and the feeder fleet on these routes mixes scrubber-fitted ships with newer dual-fuel tonnage. On the scrubber ships, the wash-water lines and overboard connections are the parts most likely to show rapid wall loss. Forest product carriers have a different priority: shippers of paper and pulp want dry, clean holds and weathertight hatch covers, because water damage to this cargo is expensive, so hatch cover plating, coamings and drainage arrangements deserve attention on ships in this trade.

jobs.h: Gauging jobs we see at Gävle
jobs.p: Most Gävle work is short and recurring. Feeder operators want a set of tanks, hatch covers or scrubber lines measured on a regular call; forest product ship owners use a loading to gauge holds and tank tops before a survey; tanker managers ask for ballast-tank readings ahead of a docking. Ice-class owners add spring work on the ice belt and bow. Where a ship calls repeatedly, we plan a programme that works through its spaces over several calls rather than trying to complete everything in one stay. Each call's readings are added to the same TM plan, so the owner ends up with one consistent record of the ship.
list: Hatch cover, coaming and scrubber wash-water line gauging on a container feeder, split across two scheduled calls.
Hold, tank-top and side-frame readings on a forest product carrier loading at Granudden, ahead of an intermediate survey.
Ballast tank and deck gauging on a product tanker at the energy port, as a pre-docking steel estimate.
Ice-belt thickness measurement and MPI at bow frames on an ice-classed feeder after a hard Bothnian winter.
On-hire condition gauging of holds and hatch covers on a general cargo ship entering a forest products charter.

logistics: The team usually lands at Stockholm Arlanda, which lies north of Stockholm and has rail connections north to Gävle, so the onward trip can be made by train or road without passing through the capital. Sweden is a Schengen state, and technicians travel from India on Schengen visas applied for as soon as the call or loading date is reasonably firm. The container terminal, Granudden and the energy port are ISPS-controlled, so the ship's agent arranges access in advance and confirms any terminal induction.

faqs.q: Can a container feeder be gauged during its Gävle call?
faqs.a: Yes, within limits set by the cargo operation. Hatch covers and coamings, scrubber lines and accessible deck structure can usually be measured while the ship works cargo, and one or two ballast tanks can be added if the crew prepares them before arrival. Larger scopes are best divided across successive calls on the same loop, which keeps the ship on schedule.

faqs.q: What happens to gauging plans when Gävle Bay is iced over?
faqs.a: The work inside the ship carries on, but schedules become less predictable. Arrivals can slip while ships wait for icebreaker assistance, so we confirm the berth time with the agent before the team travels. External shell readings are slow in frost and poor light, so we plan them for the open-water season or the docking, and use winter calls for holds, tanks and piping.

faqs.q: Can tankers at the Gävle energy port be gauged?
faqs.a: Yes, in spaces the ship can make gas-free and safe for entry, such as ballast tanks, voids and the double bottom, and on deck structure away from hazardous zones. The terminal must agree, and the ship's own permit-to-work system applies throughout. Cargo tank internals are left for a gas-free period at a yard or repair berth.

faqs.q: Where do ships trading to Gävle go for renewal surveys?
faqs.a: To docking yards elsewhere around the Baltic or the North Sea, chosen by the owner, since Gävle has no drydock for seagoing ships. Readings taken here are recorded against the TM plan's frame and strake references, so the yard and the class surveyor can use them to plan steel and close-up survey, and our team can complete the programme at the yard.
